source_review.notes: Reviewed current official PostgreSQL WAL, page-header, buffer-manager, background-writer, and checkpoint documentation/source; current official MySQL 8.4 buffer flushing and fuzzy-checkpoint documentation; the original ARIES paper; official SQLite WAL/checkpoint documentation; and the cited database textbook. All five PostgreSQL pages, the Stanford-hosted ARIES paper, and SQLite returned HTTP 200. The MySQL pages were current and readable in the research index but returned an automated-request HTTP 403 during curl calibration. Product behaviors and defaults are engine/version scoped.

evidence: Checked current/captured generation, pageLSN, imageLSN, diskLSN, and durable WAL position W for consistent version scope.
Checked distinctions among dirty, written, completed, flushed, durable, checkpoint-safe, and clean.
Checked dirty debt, replacement debt, recovery debt, steal/no-force, captured image, and fuzzy checkpoint terminology.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Storage verbs remain relative to an explicit platform and failure-domain contract; vendor terms are not treated as universal synonyms.

evidence: Recomputed the executable trace: WAL 0 blocks A:10; WAL 18 permits A:10 and B:18; re-dirtied B:25 remains dirty after the B:18 completion; WAL 18 blocks C:25; WAL 25 permits fresh B and C writes.
Verified final tuples A false/10/10, B false/25/25, and C false/25/25, with every submitted imageLSN no greater than WAL at submission.
Recomputed 60 GiB over 10 minutes as approximately 102.4 MiB/s before overhead.
Recomputed 240 GiB over 1,200 seconds as 204.8 MiB/s and, with 60 MiB/s concurrent dirty generation, 264.8 MiB/s and 35.2 MiB/s nominal headroom below 300 MiB/s.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Checkpoint arithmetic is a feasibility bound, not a controller setting or latency guarantee; fuzzy protocol scope determines which later dirties count.

evidence: Re-derived the WAL precondition W>=imageLSN for the captured image rather than the page's potentially newer current LSN.
Re-derived successful clean transition from matching tag/generation plus qualified persistence, and dirty retention from generation mismatch or absent success evidence.
Re-derived steal/no-force consequences: page files may contain uncommitted state and commits need not force all transaction pages.
Re-derived why oldest-LSN, replacement-position, heat, locality, and tenant scheduling optimize different debts.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No complete ARIES, WAL-record, checkpoint, filesystem, or device proof is claimed.

evidence: Reviewed clean/dirty, repeated dirtying, hot-page redirty, all-dirty/all-pinned pools, identity reuse, concurrent capture/update/completion, and two-writer conflicts.
Reviewed short, failed, delayed, duplicated, canceled, and uncertain I/O; ENOSPC; read-only remount; path loss; process crash; and power loss.
Reviewed volatile kernel/controller/device caches, barriers/FUA, direct versus buffered I/O, partial/torn pages, checksum detection, and unavailable replacement images.
Reviewed log saturation, checkpoint deadlines, dirty-percentage blind spots, tenant interference, queue starvation, oscillating backpressure, and recovery/backup/replica boundaries.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Failures retain or conservatively reconstruct dirty obligations; terminal storage conditions require bounded escalation rather than infinite retry.

evidence: Validated every executable submission records imageLSN<=durable WAL at that submission.
Validated B generation 1 completion advances persisted LSN to 18 without clearing generation 2 at LSN 25.
Validated the second B write and C write make all final pages clean only after WAL reaches 25.
The repository verifier matched exact nine-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
invariant_checking.notes: The model omits actual bytes, latches, threads, storage calls, sync/barriers, errors, retagging, checkpoint state, undo, and torn writes.

evidence: Reviewed the write-path argument from selection through capture, WAL forcing, immutable submission, completion, identity/version revalidation, and horizon advancement.
Reviewed cases for unchanged success, re-dirty success, failed/uncertain I/O, and stale identity.
Reviewed safety/progress separation, including WAL/storage advancement, eligible selection, bounded retry, and admission backpressure.
Reviewed the checkpoint-rate and old-page counterexamples against their stated assumptions.
proof_review.notes: No proof of scheduler optimality, starvation freedom, bounded recovery, physical durability, or implementation correctness is claimed.

evidence: Separated page-write safety from transaction commit, checkpoint completion, replica acknowledgement, and backup consistency.
Separated WAL ordering from torn-write detection/reconstruction and hardware persistence truthfulness.
Separated deterministic transition evidence, concurrency tests, crash recovery, power-cut campaigns, and production experiments.
Audited uses of durable, safe, complete, proves, invariant, recovery, and checkpoint for explicit scope.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Finite executable and fault-injection results are not promoted to universal storage or recovery proofs.

evidence: The standard-library WAL-order and generation-safe writeback model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
Seven online official/primary destinations returned HTTP 200; two current MySQL pages were indexed/read but curl-challenged with HTTP 403.
Front matter, section order, local links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and exact snippet expectations passed the pre-review draft checks.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No database engine, filesystem, device, asynchronous I/O, checkpoint, crash recovery, power-loss, corruption, replica, backup, or performance workload was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently treats writeback as WAL-ordered version propagation and connects it to steal/no-force, replacement supply, fuzzy recovery progress, storage semantics, backpressure, and failure handling.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed dirty marking, immutable capture, I/O ownership, re-dirty races, WAL forcing, storage completion/durability layers, cleaner objectives, pacing, error escalation, tenant fairness, observability, fault injection, canary rollout, and rollback.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review, executable race trace, ten distinct correctness/operations examples, and five progressive exercises move from local invariants to scheduling, control, and production assurance.

limitations: Internal authoring, official/primary-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model do not certify PostgreSQL, InnoDB, SQLite, ARIES implementations, any WAL/checkpoint/recovery protocol, filesystem/device durability, torn-write defense, writeback controller, backup/replica contract, workload result, or production fitness.
